sentenceSets.sentence: His diatribe against the new policy lasted nearly an hour, alienating colleagues who had initially been sympathetic.

answerChoices.reasoning: Complaint describes expression of dissatisfaction; while his speech involves complaint, the sentence emphasizes its sustained, bitter, and abusive character lasting nearly an hour rather than a simple expression of grievance.
Criticism describes pointing out faults; while his speech is critical, diatribe more specifically emphasizes the sustained, bitter, and often abusive nature of the speech.

Tirade is very close and often interchangeable; however, tirade may be slightly more general about angry outburst, while diatribe more specifically emphasizes sustained, often written or formal bitter speech.
Rant describes angry, uncontrolled speech; while his speech is a rant, diatribe more specifically emphasizes bitter attack and abusive tone directed at a specific target.
Objection describes formal disagreement; while he objects, diatribe emphasizes the sustained, bitter, and abusive nature rather than formal disagreement.
Protest describes strong disagreement or expression of disapproval; while applicable, diatribe emphasizes the bitter, abusive, and sustained nature more than protest.
Outburst describes sudden emotion; while his speech is an outburst, diatribe emphasizes the sustained bitter attack lasting nearly an hour rather than sudden emotion.
Argument describes presentation of reasons; while he argues, diatribe emphasizes bitter and abusive speech attacking a target rather than reasoned argument.
Praise means expressing approval; the sentence describes sustained bitter attack, opposite in tone and nature.
Endorsement means expressing support; the sentence shows alienation of sympathetic colleagues, opposite to endorsement.
Agreement describes harmony of opinion; the sentence shows his speech alienating colleagues who had been sympathetic.

answerChoices.reasoning: Essay describes a short piece of written work; while his piece is essay-length, diatribe emphasizes the bitter, abusive, and attacking nature of the criticism rather than just formal structure.
Critique describes analysis of strengths and weaknesses; while he critiques, diatribe more specifically emphasizes sustained bitter attack rather than balanced analysis.
Review describes examination and assessment; while his column reviews celebrity culture, diatribe emphasizes bitter, attacking speech more than neutral assessment.
Commentary describes explanatory remarks; while his piece provides commentary, diatribe specifically emphasizes bitter, sustained attack rather than neutral explanation.
Argument describes presentation of reasons; while he argues, diatribe emphasizes bitter, abusive attack rather than reasoned debate.
Complaint describes expression of dissatisfaction; while he complains, diatribe emphasizes sustained, bitter, and organized attack rather than simple complaint.
Opinion describes personal judgment; while he expresses opinion, diatribe emphasizes the bitter, attacking nature rather than just opinion.
Observation describes noticing something; while he makes observations, diatribe emphasizes bitter, sustained attack rather than neutral observation.
Praise means expressing approval; the sentence describes bitter attack on celebrity culture.
Flattery means offering insincere praise; the sentence attacks, not flatters.
Endorsement means expressing support; the sentence attacks celebrity culture.

answerChoices.reasoning: Speech describes any spoken address; while his address is a speech, diatribe more specifically emphasizes bitter, often attacking tone rather than neutral speech.
Address describes a formal spoken presentation; while he addresses the crowd, diatribe emphasizes the bitter, attacking quality of the speech.
Monologue describes one person speaking at length; while his presentation is monologue-like, diatribe emphasizes bitter, sustained attack rather than just one-person speech.
Discourse describes extended discussion or conversation; while he engages in discourse, diatribe more specifically emphasizes bitter, attacking nature.
Remarks describes spoken comments; while he makes remarks, diatribe emphasizes sustained, bitter, and organized attack rather than simple remarks.
Declaration describes formal announcement; while he makes declarations, diatribe emphasizes bitter, attacking tone rather than formal announcement.
Expression describes utterance or communication; while he expresses ideas, diatribe emphasizes the specific quality of bitter, sustained attack.
Oration describes formal, ceremonial speech; while he orates, diatribe emphasizes the bitter, attacking nature more than formal ceremonial quality.
Celebration describes joyful expression; the sentence describes bitter attack that moves people to tears.
Praise means expressing approval; the sentence attacks or criticizes.
Eulogy describes a speech praising someone; the sentence describes bitter, attacking speech.
